intent.title: Arcwell AI health marketing site and personal dashboard

outcome.problem: People who collect health data across wearables, symptoms, medications, and appointments still struggle to understand what changed, what is reliable, and what to discuss with a clinician.
outcome.desiredChange: A health-conscious adult can understand recent non-diagnostic patterns, inspect their sources and limits, take one appropriate next step, and prepare a concise clinician-ready summary without mistaking AI output for medical advice.
antiGoals: Diagnose a condition or replace a licensed clinician
Create anxiety through alarmist scoring or constant notifications
Hide uncertainty, source quality, data gaps, or the product safety boundary
Imitate a competitor's visual system or conversion sequence

audiences.label: Adult managing health between appointments
audiences.context: Uses a wearable and keeps occasional symptom or medication notes, but sees data in separate tools and wants useful context before an upcoming appointment.
needs: See what changed without interpreting raw charts alone
Know which source and time range support an insight
Prepare useful questions for a clinician
Control connected data and AI processing
anxieties: An AI system making an unsafe diagnosis
Sensitive health data being sold or used unexpectedly
Normal variation being presented as a crisis
Missing or delayed device data creating a false conclusion
capabilities: Can review a plain-language evidence trail
Can contact a clinician or emergency service when directed

audiences.label: Trusted family member or care partner
audiences.context: Helps another adult organize appointments, medication details, and recent changes with explicit permission.
needs: See upcoming care tasks and a concise history
anxieties: Access extending beyond the person's consent
Confusing wellness guidance with a care plan
capabilities: Can review and export a summary

primary.object: a source-grounded weekly health brief and choose an appropriate next step
primary.completionSignal: the user opens the evidence behind the weekly brief and saves or dismisses one next step

secondary.completionSignal: the user exports or copies the summary with sources, date range, questions, and AI limitations
the user reviews data sources and changes, exports, or deletes a permission
the care partner views the permitted summary without access to excluded data

values.name: grounded clarity
values.expression: Every insight names the observation, source, time range, confidence, and appropriate next step in plain language.
values.avoid: Opaque health scores, unexplained recommendations, or clinical-sounding certainty.

values.name: calm agency
values.expression: The interface prioritizes useful action and user control without manufacturing urgency.
values.avoid: Fear-based alerts, streak pressure, or moral judgment about health behavior.

values.name: visible boundaries
values.expression: Safety limits, data gaps, privacy controls, and escalation paths are part of the main experience.
values.avoid: Disclaimers hidden in legal copy or trust claims without operational detail.

experience.density: The marketing site is spacious around decisions and explicit around proof; the dashboard is information-rich but reveals evidence in layers.
experience.familiarity: Conventional navigation, forms, tables, and dialogs support a distinctive longitudinal health-thread composition.
experience.motion: Short transitions explain changes in time range or source; all meaning remains available when reduced motion is active.
experience.hierarchy: One current health brief and one next step lead the dashboard; source quality, care preparation, and data controls remain directly reachable.

criteria.signal: Visitors who understand the non-diagnostic boundary and start a connected-data trial
criteria.target: At least 10 percent of qualified marketing sessions

criteria.signal: Active users who inspect evidence behind a weekly brief before acting
Active users who save or export a clinician conversation summary before an appointment
criteria.target: At least 35 percent of users with an appointment in the next 14 days

criteria.signal: Research participants who believe Arcwell provides a diagnosis or emergency monitoring

hard.statement: The product must not claim to diagnose, treat, prevent, or monitor emergencies; every AI insight must identify its source, date range, uncertainty, and appropriate escalation boundary.
hard.verification: Claim review, interface copy audit, required evidence fields, and task walkthrough

hard.statement: Possible emergency content must bypass normal AI guidance and present direct emergency-service instructions without delay.
hard.verification: Emergency-state fixture and deterministic content assertion

hard.statement: Users must be able to inspect connected sources, understand data use, disconnect a source, export data, delete data, and manage care-partner access.
hard.verification: Control inventory, interaction test, and privacy-copy review

hard.statement: Essential health information and actions must use plain language, short explanations, descriptive headings, and progressive disclosure.
hard.verification: Content review against current HHS Health Literacy Online guidance and user comprehension testing

hard.statement: Meet WCAG 2.2 AA for tested states with complete keyboard operation and meaning that does not depend on color or motion.
hard.verification: axe-core, keyboard trace, contrast measurement, reduced-motion capture, and manual review

hard.statement: Implementation must preserve the protocol runtime and research repository outside declared paths.
hard.verification: Baseline reference, path allowlist, protected-path review, complete diff, tests, and build

soft.statement: The initial marketing and dashboard views should remain responsive on a mid-range mobile device and avoid unnecessary animation or media weight.
soft.verification: Production build inspection and browser trace

soft.statement: Demonstration data must be clearly labeled, internally consistent, and avoid implying a real person's medical record.
Selected tokens, structural decisions, evidence, and known limitations must remain retrievable for later agents.

fixed: Arcwell product name for this prototype
Marketing site and authenticated dashboard in one responsive web application
Source, date range, confidence, and safety boundary on every AI insight
Clear emergency and clinician escalation paths
forbidden: Fabricated regulatory clearance, clinical outcomes, customer logos, testimonials, or security certifications
Stock photos of clinicians or patients
Generic glowing gradient hero, glass card field, or bento feature grid
Hidden data deletion, export, or permission controls

content.sourceOfTruth: Official health-AI, privacy, accessibility, and health-literacy research captured for this run plus explicitly labeled fictional product fixtures

risks.statement: Visual polish or AI language could cause users to infer diagnosis, treatment, or clinician oversight that the prototype does not provide.
risks.control: Use non-diagnostic labels, evidence trails, uncertainty, explicit scope, and direct escalation guidance throughout the primary interface.

risks.statement: The interface could imply HIPAA coverage or security certification without an implemented service and verified operating controls.
risks.control: Describe prototype privacy controls as product behavior and avoid certification or compliance claims.

risks.statement: Users could act on an insight generated from delayed, missing, or low-quality device data.
risks.control: Show source freshness, missing periods, confidence, and a no-conclusion state before recommendations.

risks.statement: Frequent low-value warnings could increase anxiety and reduce attention to meaningful changes.
risks.control: Use one ranked brief, adjustable notification thresholds, calm language, and dismiss or snooze controls.

risks.statement: Later edits could flatten the selected health-thread direction into generic SaaS cards.
risks.control: Persist candidate decisions, tokens, evidence, and protected structural patterns in design memory.

assumptions: The prototype demonstrates product behavior with fictional data and does not process protected health information.
The first market is US adults using consumer wearables and self-entered health notes.
A real release would require legal, clinical safety, privacy, security, and user-research review beyond this design run.
Pricing and integrations shown in the prototype are illustrative and require commercial validation.
openQuestions: Which connected sources and jurisdictions should a production pilot support first?
What clinical safety governance process approves insight templates and escalation rules?
Which users benefit from care-partner access without increasing privacy risk?
What evidence threshold should suppress an AI brief entirely rather than lower confidence?

direction.thesis: Organize the product as a longitudinal health thread where every observed change, AI interpretation, source, confidence limit, and next decision remains visibly connected.

axes.composition: A vertical health thread crosses editorial marketing sections and becomes the dashboard's primary timeline, with evidence opening beside the current observation.
axes.typography: Warm humanist serif headlines pair with compact neutral sans text and tabular numerals for evidence, dates, and measurements.
axes.spatialRhythm: Large decision pauses alternate with compressed source clusters, creating a calm sequence from observation to context to action.
axes.surface: Paper-like warm fields, direct ink lines, low-radius panels, and source bands replace floating cards and decorative elevation.
axes.imagery: Original linework combines sleep, activity, symptom, and care events into one abstract longitudinal signal field without literal anatomy or stock photography.
axes.interaction: Selecting an observation reveals its evidence in place; source freshness, confidence, and next-step controls stay bound to that observation.
axes.voice: Plain, specific, measured, and explicit about what is known, inferred, missing, and outside product scope.

deliberateTradeoffs: The longitudinal structure is less immediately familiar than a standard metric-card dashboard.
Evidence remains visible, increasing information density around each important insight.
rejectedPatterns: Centered gradient hero with floating app screenshot
Chatbot as the main health interface

decisions.question: How should a user trust an AI health interpretation without treating it as a diagnosis?
decisions.option: Keep every interpretation physically connected to its observation, sources, date range, confidence, missing data, and safe next step.
decisions.rationale: Trust comes from inspectable evidence and visible boundaries rather than visual authority or a global score.
tradeoffs: The interface shows more context than a simple wellness score.
The product needs disciplined source metadata for every insight.

decisions.question: How should marketing and product feel like one system?
decisions.option: Carry the health-thread composition, source chips, and evidence language from the public page into the dashboard.
decisions.rationale: The public promise is demonstrated by the product structure instead of changing into a generic authenticated dashboard.
tradeoffs: The marketing page must explain a novel composition clearly.
The dashboard cannot rely on generic reusable card grids alone.

direction.thesis: Treat the health application as a precise personal record desk where observations, medications, appointments, sources, and actions are organized into a stable, auditable care ledger.

axes.composition: A structured two-column record desk uses a compact index, dated ledger rows, and a persistent action panel instead of a narrative timeline.
axes.typography: A restrained grotesk family uses strong labels, narrow measures, tabular numerals, and minimal display typography.
axes.spatialRhythm: Regular table rows, compact control groups, and consistent section intervals optimize scanning and comparison.
axes.surface: Cool white records, crisp rules, squared modules, and minimal color produce an administrative but approachable working surface.
axes.imagery: Small schematic data tables, calendars, and source stamps replace decorative illustration and lifestyle photography.
axes.interaction: Filters, disclosure rows, checklists, and export controls support deliberate review with few animated transitions.
axes.voice: Direct, procedural, neutral, and conservative about interpretation.

deliberateTradeoffs: The familiar record structure can feel administrative rather than emotionally supportive.
Strong scan efficiency reduces the opportunity for a distinctive narrative experience.

decisions.question: How should users manage fragmented health information reliably?
decisions.option: Use stable record categories, dated rows, visible provenance, and explicit workflow controls.
decisions.rationale: A ledger makes completeness, gaps, and ownership inspectable without requiring users to decode a visual metaphor.
tradeoffs: The experience can resemble a patient portal.
Emotional reassurance depends mainly on language rather than composition.

direction.thesis: Center the experience on one adaptive daily orientation that turns recent signals into a short, conversational check-in and a single low-pressure action.

axes.composition: A centered daily compass dominates both marketing and dashboard views, with supporting context arranged as concentric steps and a compact conversation drawer.
axes.typography: Large friendly sans headlines, short sentences, generous line height, and oversized state labels prioritize emotional approachability.
axes.spatialRhythm: Broad open fields surround one action at a time while secondary evidence waits behind progressive disclosure.
axes.surface: Soft colored zones, rounded containers, and gentle tonal transitions create an ambient coaching environment.
axes.imagery: Abstract horizon, cadence, and directional marks suggest orientation without literal medical imagery.
axes.interaction: A guided check-in asks one question at a time, then reveals the evidence and lets the user save, dismiss, or ask for clinician-preparation help.
axes.voice: Supportive, concise, conversational, and careful not to moralize behavior.

deliberateTradeoffs: Progressive disclosure can hide evidence users need before accepting a recommendation.
A conversational tone risks implying more human understanding or clinical oversight than the product provides.

decisions.question: How should the product reduce health-data overload?
decisions.option: Present one contextual orientation and one optional action before exposing the full evidence set.
decisions.rationale: A narrow daily focus reduces scanning burden and can make the product feel more usable between appointments.
tradeoffs: Evidence can become secondary to the system's framing.
The conversational experience needs stronger safeguards against anthropomorphic trust.

pairwise.rationale: Evidence Thread keeps the safety and scan clarity of the ledger while connecting observation, source, uncertainty, and next action more directly to the product's central user problem.
Daily Compass is approachable, but Evidence Thread exposes the basis and limits of AI interpretation earlier and with less risk of anthropomorphic trust.
Care Ledger is less emotionally distinctive, but its record structure makes source gaps, appointments, tasks, and data controls easier to audit than the progressively disclosed compass.
